/prompts/ai-slop-remover/.title: AI Slop Remover
/prompts/ai-slop-remover/.metaTitle: AI Slop Remover Prompt for ChatGPT — Humanize AI Writing
/prompts/ai-slop-remover/.description: This prompt turns ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini into a disciplined line editor that strips out the tell-tale patterns of AI-generated writing — binary contrasts, dramatic colon reveals, importance puffery, weasel attribution, and the banned-word list everyone recognizes (delve, leverage, tapestry) — while keeping your voice intact. Most humanizer prompts rewrite everything and sand off whatever personality your draft had. This one is built around the minimum effective edit: it fixes what sounds robotic, leaves strong human sentences alone, and reports back on exactly what it changed so you stay in control. Adapted from Peter Yang's open-source no-ai-slop editing skill (MIT licensed). Use it on newsletters, LinkedIn posts, blog articles, or any draft that started life in an AI chat window.
/prompts/ai-slop-remover/.metaDescription: Free ChatGPT prompt that removes AI slop — banned words, binary contrasts, puffery — while keeping your voice. Edit any draft so it sounds human.
/prompts/ai-slop-remover/.promptText:
You are a sharp human editor. Your job is to remove AI-sounding patterns from my draft while preserving my point and my personal voice. Do not turn distinctive writing into generic polished prose.

The draft is for: [AUDIENCE]
It will be published as: [FORMAT]

My draft:
[DRAFT]

Editing rules:
1. Make the minimum effective edit. Fix AI patterns, repetition, and unclear passages. Leave strong human sentences alone. The edited draft should still sound like me.
2. Cut these words entirely: delve, foster, leverage, utilize, facilitate, empower, streamline, robust, cutting-edge, game changer, tapestry, realm, beacon, multifaceted, meticulous, paramount, transformative, elevate, embark, harness, ever-evolving.
3. Cut empty phrases like "it's worth noting," "at the end of the day," "in today's world," "let's dive in," and "the reality is" when they delay the point.
4. Remove these AI patterns wherever they appear:
- Binary contrasts ("It's not X. It's Y.") — state the point directly instead
- Throat-clearing openers ("Here's the thing...") — cut them and lead with the point
- Faux-insight setups ("What nobody tells you...") — let the claim stand on its own
- Dramatic colon reveals ("The best part: it learns.") — rewrite as a plain sentence
- Trailing -ing analysis ("...highlighting the team's commitment") — replace with the actual consequence or cut
- Importance puffery ("marks a pivotal moment," "stands as a testament") — state the fact and let the reader judge
- Weasel attribution ("experts agree," "studies show") — name the source or flag it for me, never invent one
- Negative listing ("Not a tool. Not a platform. A movement.") — just say what it is
- Dramatic fragments ("That's it. That's the whole thing.") — use complete sentences
- Fake-profound final lines that end on a cute metaphor — delete them and end on the last concrete point
- Summary-recap endings ("In conclusion...") — the reader was just there
5. Use active voice with human subjects. Replace weak verb phrases with direct verbs ("made a decision" becomes "decided").
6. Keep concrete details exactly as written. Never smooth a specific number, name, or date into a vague claim, and never invent claims, stats, or examples I did not provide.
7. Keep my edge. Preserve strong opinions, blunt language, humor, fragments, and asides that sound like me. Use at most 1-2 em dashes in the whole piece.

Output format:
1. The full edited draft
2. A short "What changed" section listing the patterns you removed and why
3. Any claims that need a source, flagged as questions for me

variables.example: Startup founders who subscribe to my newsletter

variables.description: Where and how it will be published
The full draft you want edited
variables.example: Here's the thing: AI tools aren't just changing marketing. They're transforming it. Our new workflow leverages cutting-edge automation, highlighting our commitment to efficiency...

tips: Paste your whole draft, not a paragraph at a time — the editor needs the full piece to catch repeated sentence shapes and a weak ending
Fill in AUDIENCE and FORMAT honestly; a LinkedIn post and a technical doc need different levels of polish
If the output flags a claim as needing a source, add the real source rather than letting the model soften the claim
Run the edited draft through the companion AI Slop Detector prompt if you want a second-pass audit without another rewrite

/prompts/business-plan-executive-summary.title: Claude Business Plan Executive Summary Prompt
/prompts/business-plan-executive-summary.metaTitle: Claude Business Plan Prompt for Executive Summaries
/prompts/business-plan-executive-summary.description: Use this Claude business plan prompt to draft an investor-ready executive summary for a startup, small business, lender packet, pitch deck, or accelerator application. The prompt turns your company details, target market, traction, financial projections, and funding ask into a clear business plan executive summary that covers the sections investors and lenders expect to see. It is built for founders who need a stronger first draft before polishing numbers, claims, and market evidence.
/prompts/business-plan-executive-summary.metaDescription: Use this Claude business plan prompt to write an investor-ready executive summary for funding, lender packets, pitch decks, and startup planning.
/prompts/business-plan-executive-summary.promptText: You are a seasoned business consultant who has helped 200+ startups secure funding. Write an investor-ready executive summary for [COMPANY_NAME], a [BUSINESS_MODEL] startup in the [INDUSTRY] industry. The company solves [PROBLEM] for [TARGET_MARKET] by offering [SOLUTION]. Include these sections: Company Overview (2-3 sentences), Problem Statement, Solution, Target Market size and characteristics, Revenue Model, Competitive Advantage, Current Traction (use [TRACTION_METRICS] as data points), Financial Projections summary for 3 years, and Funding Ask of [FUNDING_AMOUNT] with planned allocation. Keep the entire summary under 800 words, write in a polished Claude-friendly business-plan style, and make every sentence earn its place.

variables.example: generic nutrition advice that ignores individual health conditions, genetics, and lifestyle
health-conscious adults aged 25-55 managing chronic conditions through diet
an AI-powered meal planning app that creates personalized nutrition plans based on bloodwork, genetic data, and health goals
12,000 paid subscribers, $45K MRR, 94% month-over-month retention, partnerships with 3 major lab testing companies

tips: Lead with your strongest traction metric to hook the reader immediately
Quantify your market size with a credible TAM/SAM/SOM breakdown
Tailor the tone based on your audience: VCs want growth metrics, banks want stability
Ask Claude for a lender version, investor version, and accelerator version so you can compare the framing before final edits
